references.title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG
references.contribution: Organizes agentic RAG architectures and design trade-offs, including planning, tool use, memory, and adaptive retrieval.
references.limits: A survey and taxonomy do not establish that any particular project architecture improves task outcomes.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk implements a bounded research workflow with explicit tool contracts and directly measured citation checks; it does not propose a taxonomy.
references.date_note: First release is 2025; this record explicitly cites the revised 2026 v4 with its current five-author list.
references.reference: A. Singh, A. Ehtesham, S. Kumar, T. T. Khoei, and A. V. Vasilakos, "Agentic retrieval-augmented generation: A survey on agentic RAG," arXiv:2501.09136v4, Apr. 2026, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2501.09136.

references.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
references.venue: arXiv preprint (venue not independently verified here)
references.contribution: Trains interleaved reasoning and search-query behavior through reinforcement learning with retrieved-token masking and outcome rewards.
references.limits: The method requires policy training; its QA results cannot be transferred to an untrained project agent.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk uses a fixed local model and bounded tool orchestration, without reinforcement-learning training or claims to reproduce Search-R1.
references.reference: B. Jin et al., "Search-R1: Training LLMs to reason and leverage search engines with reinforcement learning," arXiv:2503.09516, 2025, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2503.09516.

references.title: An Empirical Study on Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning-Search Interleaved LLM Agents
references.contribution: Studies how reward design, model scale and initialization, and search-engine choice affect trained reasoning-search agents.
references.limits: Its conclusions concern the studied RL settings and do not determine the best settings for a small frozen-model application.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk isolates retrieval and auditing in application ablations instead of studying RL reward formulations.
references.reference: B. Jin, J. Yoon, P. Kargupta, S. O. Arik, and J. Han, "An empirical study on reinforcement learning for reasoning-search interleaved LLM agents," arXiv:2505.15117, 2025, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2505.15117.

references.title: DeepResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Reinforcement Learning in Real-world Environments
references.contribution: Trains deep-research agents through reinforcement learning on authentic web interactions with specialized browsing agents.
references.limits: Large-scale policy training and open-web evaluation are outside the scope and compute budget of the proposed project.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk focuses on a small curated corpus and auditable evidence records instead of training open-web research policies.
references.reference: Y. Zheng et al., "DeepResearcher: Scaling deep research via reinforcement learning in real-world environments," in Proc. EMNLP, 2025, pp. 414-431, doi: 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.22.

references.title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
references.contribution: Introduces 1,266 difficult browsing questions with short, verifiable answers to test persistent information seeking.
references.limits: Short-answer browsing performance does not by itself measure faithful long-form synthesis or realistic user-query coverage.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk evaluates a smaller disclosed corpus and evidence audit behavior, not BrowseComp-level open-web search capability.
references.reference: J. Wei et al., "BrowseComp: A simple yet challenging benchmark for browsing agents," arXiv:2504.12516, 2025, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2504.12516.

references.title: CiteEval: Principle-Driven Citation Evaluation for Source Attribution
references.venue: Proceedings of ACL 2025, Volume 1: Long Papers
references.contribution: Develops multidimensional citation assessment, the human-annotated CiteBench benchmark, and model-based CiteEval-Auto metrics.
references.limits: A deterministic source-ID and quotation check is much narrower than the paper's contextual citation-quality evaluation.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk checks inspectable source and quote properties and reports human support labels separately; it does not reproduce CiteEval.
references.reference: Y. Xu et al., "CiteEval: Principle-driven citation evaluation for source attribution," in Proc. ACL, vol. 1, 2025, pp. 32759-32778, doi: 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.1574.

references.title: DeepResearch Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Deep Research Agents
references.venue: arXiv preprint; later venue not used in this citation
references.contribution: Introduces 100 expert-created research tasks across 22 fields and evaluation methods for report quality and citation accuracy.
references.limits: Benchmark-scale expert tasks and judge protocols exceed the coverage of a small classroom evaluation.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk publishes a small task list and component measurements rather than claiming comparable benchmark performance.
references.reference: M. Du, B. Xu, C. Zhu, X. Wang, and Z. Mao, "DeepResearch Bench: A comprehensive benchmark for deep research agents," arXiv:2506.11763, 2025, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2506.11763.

references.title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
references.contribution: Uses heterogeneous retrieval-derived training data and gated rewards to jointly train evidence grounding and abstention.
references.limits: Its reinforcement-learning results do not validate prompt-only abstention or deterministic audits in a different application.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk uses a frozen model and explicit application checks; it evaluates abstention without claiming GRACE's learned policy.
references.reference: Y. Zhao, J. Zhu, Z. Ding, and X. Li, "GRACE: Reinforcement learning for grounded response and abstention under contextual evidence," arXiv:2601.04525, 2026, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2601.04525.

references.title: DeepResearch Bench II: Diagnosing Deep Research Agents via Rubrics from Expert Reports
references.contribution: Builds expert-grounded research tasks with fine-grained binary rubrics for information recall, analysis, and presentation.
references.limits: Its expert-review effort and broad research tasks are not reproduced by the classroom project.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk uses a small explicit rubric and records individual outcomes rather than claiming broad expert-level research ability.
references.reference: R. Li, M. Du, B. Xu, C. Zhu, X. Wang, and Z. Mao, "DeepResearch Bench II: Diagnosing deep research agents via rubrics from expert reports," arXiv:2601.08536v3, Sep. 2026, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2601.08536.

references.title: Atlas: Customizing Large Language Models for Reliable Bibliographic Retrieval and Verification
references.venue: Proceedings of the Third Workshop for Artificial Intelligence for Scientific Publications
references.contribution: Compares Crossref resolution, generic GPT prompting, and verification-guided prompting for bibliographic retrieval quality.
references.limits: Bibliographic field accuracy is different from establishing that a response's substantive claims are supported by paper passages.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk must acknowledge this close overlap; its scope additionally includes local evidence passages, visible tool traces, and abstention checks.
references.date_note: First known publication date is the workshop's 23 December 2025 date printed on the PDF; no earlier preprint is asserted.
references.reference: A. Kodali, H. Xu, W. Zhang, and X. Qin, "Atlas: Customizing large language models for reliable bibliographic retrieval and verification," in Proc. WASP, 2025, pp. 121-126, doi: 10.18653/v1/2025.wasp-main.14.

references.title: Data-Centric Perspectives on Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
references.contribution: Organizes agentic-RAG data collection, task construction, evaluation, and training-data enhancement into a data lifecycle.
references.limits: A survey's dataset taxonomy is background, not direct experimental validation of EvidenceDesk's small test set.
references.project_difference: EvidenceDesk supplies disclosed classroom tasks and component traces instead of proposing a broad data-lifecycle survey.
references.date_note: July 2026 venue publication is verified; an earlier preprint date was not established. The other ten entries independently meet the date requirement.
references.reference: J. Deng et al., "Data-centric perspectives on agentic retrieval-augmented generation: A survey," in Findings ACL, 2026, pp. 1570-1588, doi: 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-acl.78.

date_policy: Ten papers have verified 2025-2026 first-known dates; the eleventh has a verified 2026 venue publication. Versions and first releases are recorded separately.
